---
title: "Menus"
description: "Every command in the Frame Job, File, Edit, Insert, Track, Mark, View, Window and Help menus, with its shortcut and when it's available."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page lists every command in the menu bar, in menu order, with its shortcut and what has to be true for it to be available. Use it to find a command's key, or to work out why an item is greyed out. Each row says what the command does in a few words, and the page it links to has the full story.

The menu bar reads Frame Job, File, Edit, Insert, Clip, Track, Mark, View, Window, Help. The Clip menu is long enough to have [its own page](/reference/clip-menu/).

## How to read these tables

| Symbol | Key |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘ | Command |
| ⌥ | Option |
| ⇧ | Shift |
| ⌃ | Control |
| ⌫ | Delete |
| ↩ | Return |
| ⎋ | Escape |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | The arrow keys |

- **(key)** after a shortcut means a bare key the menu doesn't draw: <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd>, <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd>, <kbd>N</kbd> and <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>. The editor handles these itself rather than the menu, so a text field can never lose the letter to them. They work in the editor window and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/), and not while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open.
- **A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed out.**
- **Always** in the last column means whenever a project window is in front with no sheet on it. While a sheet is up, every command that acts on the project is greyed out, and so is every such command when no project window is open.
- **The current track** is the track of the first selected clip. With nothing selected it's the front-most track.
- <kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> are switched off while you type in a text field, so they keep their usual text-editing meaning there.

macOS may add items of its own to these menus. Those aren't listed. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has every key, including the ones with no menu item.

## Frame Job menu

| Item | Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **About Frame Job** | | Shows the version and credits panel, with the Frame Job mark. |
| **Check for Updates…** | | Asks whether a newer Frame Job has been published and offers to install it. Greyed while a check is running. It's only in the copy downloaded from GitHub, and a build from source doesn't have it. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/). |
| **Settings…** | <kbd>⌘,</kbd> | Opens the [Settings](/reference/settings/) window. It works with no project open. |
| **Hide Frame Job** | <kbd>⌘H</kbd> | Hides the app. |
| **Hide Others** | <kbd>⌥⌘H</kbd> | Hides every other app. |
| **Show All** | | Shows hidden apps again. |
| **Quit Frame Job** | <kbd>⌘Q</kbd> | Quits. Projects with unsaved work are dealt with first, as on any Mac. |

Two things can stop a quit:

- **A recording is running.** The quit is cancelled and the recording's controls are put in front of you. Stop the recording first. See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/#quit-during-a-recording).
- **The Export Queue is busy.** An alert reads "An export is still being written." It says what's running and how many more are waiting, and **Quit Anyway** stops the export and deletes the partly written file. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#quit-with-jobs-in-the-queue).

Only the queue is guarded. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves a half-written file behind.

No agent tool checks for updates or quits the app.

## File menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['new_project', 'record_screen', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'open_project', 'close_project', 'save_project']}
/>

The first groups make, open, close and save projects, and start or stop a recording.

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **New Project** | <kbd>⌘N</kbd> | Opens a new, empty project window straight away, 1920×1080 at 30 fps. See [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/). | With or without a project open |
| **New Recording…** | <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> | Opens the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). While a recording runs the item reads **Stop Recording** and stops it, whether the panel or an agent started it. | With or without a project open |
| **Pause Recording** | | Pauses the running recording. The item reads **Resume Recording** while paused. It beeps if the recording can't pause or resume. | During a recording |
| **New Project from Range…** | | Opens the in/out range as a new untitled project, with its media's caches and its graphics. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). | An in/out range is set and no nest is open |
| **Make Vertical Version…** | | Makes a 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version of the timeline, as a new untitled project or in this one. See [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/). | The project has a clip, no nest is open and no recording is running |
| **Open…** | <kbd>⌘O</kbd> | Opens a project or a media file. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/). | With or without a project open |
| **Open Recent ▸** | | Lists recently opened documents, filled in by macOS, then **Clear Menu**. | With or without a project open |
| **Close** | <kbd>⌘W</kbd> | Closes the window, asking about unsaved work. | |
| **Save** | <kbd>⌘S</kbd> | Saves the project. | |
| **Duplicate** | <kbd>⇧⌘S</kbd> | Opens a copy of the project as a new, untitled document. | |
| **Save As…** | <kbd>⌥⇧⌘S</kbd> | Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> and **Duplicate** becomes this. It writes the project to a new package. | |
| **Rename…** | | Renames the project's package. | |
| **Move To…** | | Moves the project's package to another folder. | |
| **Revert To ▸** | | Goes back to the last saved version, or browses earlier versions of the package. | |
| **Share** | | Opens the macOS Share menu for the project. | |

Projects autosave, so macOS gives this menu its own document commands: **Duplicate** in place of **Save As…**, and **Revert To ▸** in place of **Revert to Saved**, with **Rename…**, **Move To…** and **Share** beside them. macOS also decides when these and **Close** and **Save** are available. [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) has what each one does.

## File menu: media, captions, graphics

<AtAGlance
  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions', 'transcribe', 'export_captions', 'relay_captions', 'consolidate_media', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'rename_graphic', 'delete_graphic', 'restore_graphic']}
/>

The middle group brings in media, captions, fonts and pictures, and looks after the project's graphics. Only **Add Media…** has a key, because a menu key with no modifier would take a letter from the editor.

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Media…** | <kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd> | Imports files into the project's Media list. Several at once are one undo step. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/). | Always |
| **Import Captions…** | | Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new text track. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/). | Always |
| **Generate Captions…** | | Makes captions from speech. See [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/). | A clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on |
| **Export Captions…** | | Writes a caption track out as a file. See [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/). | The project has a caption track, meaning a track whose clips are all text clips |
| **Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** | | Re-pages the word caption tracks for the current canvas, keeping every correction, as one undo step, "Re-lay Captions". See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/). | The timeline, or the open nest, has a word caption track Frame Job can re-lay, and no recording is running |
| **Consolidate Media…** | | Copies the project's media into the project package. An untitled project asks you to save first. See [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/). | The project has media |
| **Add Font to Graphics…** | | Adds a `.ttf` or `.otf` font that graphics can use. It can't be undone. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/). | Always |
| **Add Image to Graphics…** | | Adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ picture that graphics can use. It can't be undone. | Always |
| **Rename Graphic…** | | Renames one of the project's graphics, and every clip using it follows. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). | The project has graphics and no nest is open |
| **Delete Graphic…** | | Deletes a graphic no clip uses. Frame Job won't delete one a clip is using. It isn't an undo step. | The project has graphics |
| **Restore Graphic Version…** | | Brings back an earlier version of a graphic. It isn't an undo step. | An earlier version of a graphic is kept |

## File menu: export

<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export', 'render_frame']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Export…** | <kbd>⌘E</kbd> | Opens the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/). It always exports the timeline, even with a nest open. The toolbar's **Export…** button does the same. | The project isn't empty |
| **Save Frame…** | <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd> | Saves the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC still. Inside a nest it saves the frame the canvas shows. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). | The timeline you're editing has a duration |

## Edit menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['undo', 'redo', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'duplicate', 'delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Undo** | <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> | Undoes the last edit. The item names it, for example **Undo Move Clips** or **Undo Ripple Delete**. See [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/). | There's something to undo |
| **Redo** | <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> | Redoes it, named the same way. Any new edit clears what could be redone. | There's something to redo |
| **Cut** | <kbd>⌘X</kbd> | Copies the selected clips and removes them, leaving a gap. If the copy fails, nothing is removed. See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/). | Something is selected |
| **Copy** | <kbd>⌘C</kbd> | Copies the selected clips. A selection across several tracks pastes back onto as many lanes. Pasted into another app, it's a short text summary. | Something is selected |
| **Paste** | <kbd>⌘V</kbd> | Pastes clips at the playhead, the earliest there and the others keeping their offsets. Nothing needs to be selected. It works between projects, matching media by path. | The clipboard holds Frame Job clips |
| **Paste Attributes** | <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd> | Puts the copied clip's look onto the selected clips. Only the earliest copied clip is read. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/). | Frame Job clips are copied and something is selected |
| **Paste Graphic Properties** | | Puts the copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips that use the same graphic. It beeps if the copied clip isn't a graphic. See [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/). | Frame Job clips are copied and a graphic clip is selected |
| **Duplicate** | <kbd>⌘D</kbd> | Copies the selected clips and places the copies after them. See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/). | Something is selected |
| **Delete** | <kbd>⌫</kbd> | Removes the selection and leaves a gap. With nothing selected it lifts the in/out range. With an action selected it removes that action, not its clip. With words selected in the Transcript tab it ripples them out. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/). | Something is selected, a range is set, or words are selected. Off while text is being edited, and while the curve plot holds a selected point, where <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point |
| **Ripple Delete** | <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | Removes the selection, or the in/out range when nothing is selected, and closes the gap. Words selected in the Transcript tab go first. | Something is selected, a range is set, or words are selected. Off while text is being edited |
| **Insert at Playhead** | | Inserts the file selected in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/), pushing later clips along. One undo step, "Insert". See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). | A file is selected in the Media tab, and it isn't a LUT |
| **Overwrite at Playhead** | | Places that file over whatever is there. One undo step, "Overwrite". | A file is selected in the Media tab, and it isn't a LUT |
| **Select All** | <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Selects every clip in the timeline you're editing. With the Transcript tab's words in focus, it selects every word. | Always |
| **Select After Playhead** | <kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd> | Selects every clip that starts at or after the playhead. | Always |
| **Select All on Track** | | Selects every clip on the current track. It beeps when the track is empty. | The timeline has clips |

Selecting adds no undo step. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).

## Insert menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_adjustment_clip', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'text_behind_subject']}
/>

No item in this menu has a key.

| Item | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Adjustment Clip** | Adds an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) over the in/out range. Without a range it covers the selected clips' span, and without a selection the whole timeline. It lands on the front track when it fits, and otherwise on a new front track named "Adjustment". One undo step. | No nest is open and the timeline isn't empty |
| **Graphic…** | Opens the Graphic dialog: the bundled templates by category, **This Project**'s own graphics and a looping preview, with **Insert**, **From File…** (a `.js` file, or a `.fjgraphic` to import) and **Export…** (saves the chosen one as a `.fjgraphic`). See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). | Always |
| **Text Behind Subject** | Puts a title on a new "Behind Subject" track above the camera clip at the playhead, behind the person, for 4 s or the rest of the clip. It turns [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on with Keep background when the clip doesn't have it. One undo step. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). | No nest is open, and a clip of a video file or a picture plays at the playhead with its picture on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track |

## Clip menu

The Clip menu sits between Insert and Track. See [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/).

## Track menu

<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'set_track', 'move_track']} />

Everything here but **New Track** and **Remove Empty Tracks** acts on the [current track](#how-to-read-these-tables). To act on a particular track, use that track's [context menu](/reference/context-menus/). Every item is available whenever a project window is in front with no sheet on it.

| Item | Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **New Track** | <kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd> | Adds a track at the front, the top lane. See [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/). |
| **Remove Track** | | Removes the current track. If it still holds clips you're asked first and told how many go with it, with **Remove** and **Cancel**. The last track can't be removed. |
| **Remove Empty Tracks** | | Removes every track that has no clips, keeping one if they're all empty. It beeps when there's nothing to remove. |
| **Hide Video** | | Hides or shows the track's picture. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| **Mute Audio** | | Mutes or unmutes the track's sound. Mute wins over Solo. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
| **Lock Track** | | Locks or unlocks the track, so its clips can't be edited. |
| **Solo** | | Plays only this track's sound. It's audio only. A checkmark shows when it's on, because a soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest. |
| **Mix…** | | Opens the track's mix panel: volume, pan, compressor and limiter. A timeline has one panel at a time, so opening it on another track closes the first. Inside an open nest its dynamics are disabled. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). |
| **Matte ▸** | | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**. Makes the track a matte that cuts the track behind it, and a checkmark shows the mode. One undo step, "Track Matte", and choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |

**Hide Video**, **Mute Audio** and **Lock Track** show no checkmark here. The track's context menu shows one.

## Mark menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_range', 'set_playhead']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Marker** | <kbd>M</kbd> (key) | Adds a marker at the playhead, snapped to a frame. A second marker on the same frame beeps. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/). | No nest is open |
| **Set In** | <kbd>I</kbd> (key) | Sets the in point at the playhead. With no Out yet, the range runs to the end of the timeline. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/). | Always |
| **Set Out** | <kbd>O</kbd> (key) | Sets the out point at the playhead. With no In yet, the range starts at 0. | Always |
| **Clear Range** | <kbd>⌥X</kbd> | Clears the in/out range. | A range is set |
| **Next Marker** | | Moves the playhead to the next marker and pauses. It beeps past the last one. | The project has markers and no nest is open |
| **Previous Marker** | | Moves the playhead to the previous marker and pauses. It beeps before the first one. | The project has markers and no nest is open |

Setting In or Out adds no undo step.

## View menu

These items set how the window looks. Zoom always acts on the canvas. To zoom the timeline, use the timeline bar's controls or the [gestures](/reference/gestures/).

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Zoom In** | <kbd>⌘+</kbd> or <kbd>⌘=</kbd> | Zooms the canvas in one step. The steps are Fit, 50 %, 100 % and 200 %. See [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). | The canvas is below 200 % |
| **Zoom Out** | <kbd>⌘-</kbd> | Zooms the canvas out one step. | The canvas isn't at Fit |
| **Zoom to Fit** | <kbd>⌘0</kbd> | Fits the canvas to the preview again. | The canvas isn't at Fit |
| **Fit Timeline** | <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> (key) | Zooms the timeline to show the whole project and scrolls to the start. See [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/). | Always |
| **Snapping** | <kbd>N</kbd> (key) | Turns [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) on or off for the timeline and the canvas. A checkmark shows when it's on. | Always |
| **Safe Areas** | | Shows or hides the [safe-area guides](/canvas/safe-areas/) on the canvas, with a checkmark. | Always |
| **Hide Inspector** | <kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd> | Hides the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/). The item reads **Show Inspector** while it's hidden. | Always |
| **Transcript** | <kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd> | Shows the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), ready for its keys, showing the inspector first if it's hidden. | Always |
| **Assistant** | <kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd> | Shows the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/) tab and puts the cursor in its message field, showing the inspector first if it's hidden. | Always |
| **Timeline Track Height ▸** | | **Small**, **Medium** or **Large**. Sets the height of the timeline rows, and a checkmark marks the current one. A lane's height also depends on what it holds. See [Track height](/timeline/track-height/). | Always |

**Snapping**, **Safe Areas**, **Hide Inspector** and **Timeline Track Height** are [remembered between launches](/reference/remembered-choices/).

## View menu: preview

<AtAGlance tools={['render_frame', 'get_media_analysis']} />

These items change what you see in the preview, and none of them changes an export or a saved frame.

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Preview Quality ▸** | | **Full**, **Half** or **Quarter**. The preview's render size while you play, with a checkmark on the current row. It keeps the canvas's exact aspect ratio, so an awkward canvas size can render larger than the row's fraction. See [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/). | Always |
| **Preview Window** | <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd> | Opens a second window showing the picture without overlays, handles or chrome. Choose it again to close it, and a checkmark says it's on screen. See [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). | Always |
| **Show Ungraded** | <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd> | Shows the preview as if no clip were graded, with a tag on the preview saying so. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). | Always |
| **Show Selection** | | Shows which pixels the selected adjustment clip's qualifier picks. It follows another adjustment clip when the selection moves to one, and turns off when none is selected. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/). | An adjustment clip is selected, or it's already on |
| **Show SDR Version** | | Shows an HDR project's SDR version. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). | Always |
| **Show Subjects** | | Draws the selected clip's faces, people and salient regions at the playhead, from what's already been analysed. It never starts an analysis, so a clip with none shows "Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it". See [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/). | Always |
| **Scopes** | <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> | Shows the scopes panel beside the preview. A new window starts with Waveform over Vectorscope. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/). | Always |
| **Loudness Meter** | <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd> | Shows the live loudness column beside the preview: momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and the true peak of what plays. It has a Reset, and the meter measures whether or not it's showing. See [The Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/). | Always |

**Preview Quality** is remembered between launches. **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection**, **Show SDR Version**, **Show Subjects**, **Scopes** and **Loudness Meter** belong to the window and aren't remembered.

## Window menu

<AtAGlance tools={['export_status', 'cancel_export']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Minimize** | <kbd>⌘M</kbd> | Minimizes the front window to the Dock. |
| **Zoom** | | Makes the window larger or smaller. This is the window's zoom, not the canvas's. |
| **Export Queue** | | Opens the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) window. A running export doesn't stop when the window closes. |
| **Bring All to Front** | | Brings all Frame Job windows to the front. |
| Each open window | | Brings that window forward, as in any Mac app. |

The open windows are listed at the end of the menu. Settings is listed there while it's open, so you can bring it back from behind other windows. The Export Queue, the Preview Window and the recorder panel aren't listed.

## Help menu

<AtAGlance tools="graphic_reference" />

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Frame Job Help** | The standard macOS help item. The app doesn't ship a help book, so macOS answers with its own message. This site is the help. |
| **Graphics Reference** | Opens the bundled graphics scripting reference in your default Markdown app. It works with no project open. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/). |

## Related

---
title: "Menus"
description: "Every command in the Frame Job, File, Edit, Insert, Track, Mark, View, Window and Help menus, with its shortcut and when it's available."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page lists every command in the menu bar, in menu order, with its shortcut and what has to be true for it to be available. Use it to find a command's key, or to work out why an item is greyed out. Each row says what the command does in a few words, and the page it links to has the full story.

The menu bar reads Frame Job, File, Edit, Insert, Clip, Track, Mark, View, Window, Help. The Clip menu is long enough to have [its own page](/reference/clip-menu/).

## How to read these tables

| Symbol | Key |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘ | Command |
| ⌥ | Option |
| ⇧ | Shift |
| ⌃ | Control |
| ⌫ | Delete |
| ↩ | Return |
| ⎋ | Escape |
| ← → ↑ ↓ | The arrow keys |

- **(key)** after a shortcut means a bare key the menu doesn't draw: <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd>, <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd>, <kbd>N</kbd> and <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>. The editor handles these itself rather than the menu, so a text field can never lose the letter to them. They work in the editor window and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/), and not while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open.
- **A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed out.**
- **Always** in the last column means whenever a project window is in front with no sheet on it. While a sheet is up, every command that acts on the project is greyed out, and so is every such command when no project window is open.
- **The current track** is the track of the first selected clip. With nothing selected it's the front-most track.
- <kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> are switched off while you type in a text field, so they keep their usual text-editing meaning there.

macOS may add items of its own to these menus. Those aren't listed. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has every key, including the ones with no menu item.

## Frame Job menu

| Item | Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **About Frame Job** | | Shows the version and credits panel, with the Frame Job mark. |
| **Check for Updates…** | | Asks whether a newer Frame Job has been published and offers to install it. Greyed while a check is running. It's only in the copy downloaded from GitHub, and a build from source doesn't have it. See [Updates](/getting-started/updates/). |
| **Settings…** | <kbd>⌘,</kbd> | Opens the [Settings](/reference/settings/) window. It works with no project open. |
| **Hide Frame Job** | <kbd>⌘H</kbd> | Hides the app. |
| **Hide Others** | <kbd>⌥⌘H</kbd> | Hides every other app. |
| **Show All** | | Shows hidden apps again. |
| **Quit Frame Job** | <kbd>⌘Q</kbd> | Quits. Projects with unsaved work are dealt with first, as on any Mac. |

Two things can stop a quit:

- **A recording is running.** The quit is cancelled and the recording's controls are put in front of you. Stop the recording first. See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/#quit-during-a-recording).
- **The Export Queue is busy.** An alert reads "An export is still being written." It says what's running and how many more are waiting, and **Quit Anyway** stops the export and deletes the partly written file. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#quit-with-jobs-in-the-queue).

Only the queue is guarded. Quitting while an **Export…** progress sheet is writing doesn't ask, and leaves a half-written file behind.

No agent tool checks for updates or quits the app.

## File menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['new_project', 'record_screen', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'open_project', 'close_project', 'save_project']}
/>

The first groups make, open, close and save projects, and start or stop a recording.

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **New Project** | <kbd>⌘N</kbd> | Opens a new, empty project window straight away, 1920×1080 at 30 fps. See [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/). | With or without a project open |
| **New Recording…** | <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> | Opens the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). While a recording runs the item reads **Stop Recording** and stops it, whether the panel or an agent started it. | With or without a project open |
| **Pause Recording** | | Pauses the running recording. The item reads **Resume Recording** while paused. It beeps if the recording can't pause or resume. | During a recording |
| **New Project from Range…** | | Opens the in/out range as a new untitled project, with its media's caches and its graphics. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). | An in/out range is set and no nest is open |
| **Make Vertical Version…** | | Makes a 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version of the timeline, as a new untitled project or in this one. See [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/). | The project has a clip, no nest is open and no recording is running |
| **Open…** | <kbd>⌘O</kbd> | Opens a project or a media file. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/). | With or without a project open |
| **Open Recent ▸** | | Lists recently opened documents, filled in by macOS, then **Clear Menu**. | With or without a project open |
| **Close** | <kbd>⌘W</kbd> | Closes the window, asking about unsaved work. | |
| **Save** | <kbd>⌘S</kbd> | Saves the project. | |
| **Duplicate** | <kbd>⇧⌘S</kbd> | Opens a copy of the project as a new, untitled document. | |
| **Save As…** | <kbd>⌥⇧⌘S</kbd> | Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> and **Duplicate** becomes this. It writes the project to a new package. | |
| **Rename…** | | Renames the project's package. | |
| **Move To…** | | Moves the project's package to another folder. | |
| **Revert To ▸** | | Goes back to the last saved version, or browses earlier versions of the package. | |
| **Share** | | Opens the macOS Share menu for the project. | |

Projects autosave, so macOS gives this menu its own document commands: **Duplicate** in place of **Save As…**, and **Revert To ▸** in place of **Revert to Saved**, with **Rename…**, **Move To…** and **Share** beside them. macOS also decides when these and **Close** and **Save** are available. [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) has what each one does.

## File menu: media, captions, graphics

<AtAGlance
  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions', 'transcribe', 'export_captions', 'relay_captions', 'consolidate_media', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'rename_graphic', 'delete_graphic', 'restore_graphic']}
/>

The middle group brings in media, captions, fonts and pictures, and looks after the project's graphics. Only **Add Media…** has a key, because a menu key with no modifier would take a letter from the editor.

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Media…** | <kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd> | Imports files into the project's Media list. Several at once are one undo step. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/). | Always |
| **Import Captions…** | | Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new text track. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/). | Always |
| **Generate Captions…** | | Makes captions from speech. See [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/). | A clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on |
| **Export Captions…** | | Writes a caption track out as a file. See [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/). | The project has a caption track, meaning a track whose clips are all text clips |
| **Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** | | Re-pages the word caption tracks for the current canvas, keeping every correction, as one undo step, "Re-lay Captions". See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/). | The timeline, or the open nest, has a word caption track Frame Job can re-lay, and no recording is running |
| **Consolidate Media…** | | Copies the project's media into the project package. An untitled project asks you to save first. See [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/). | The project has media |
| **Add Font to Graphics…** | | Adds a `.ttf` or `.otf` font that graphics can use. It can't be undone. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/). | Always |
| **Add Image to Graphics…** | | Adds a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ picture that graphics can use. It can't be undone. | Always |
| **Rename Graphic…** | | Renames one of the project's graphics, and every clip using it follows. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). | The project has graphics and no nest is open |
| **Delete Graphic…** | | Deletes a graphic no clip uses. Frame Job won't delete one a clip is using. It isn't an undo step. | The project has graphics |
| **Restore Graphic Version…** | | Brings back an earlier version of a graphic. It isn't an undo step. | An earlier version of a graphic is kept |

## File menu: export

<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export', 'render_frame']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Export…** | <kbd>⌘E</kbd> | Opens the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/). It always exports the timeline, even with a nest open. The toolbar's **Export…** button does the same. | The project isn't empty |
| **Save Frame…** | <kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd> | Saves the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC still. Inside a nest it saves the frame the canvas shows. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). | The timeline you're editing has a duration |

## Edit menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['undo', 'redo', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'duplicate', 'delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Undo** | <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> | Undoes the last edit. The item names it, for example **Undo Move Clips** or **Undo Ripple Delete**. See [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/). | There's something to undo |
| **Redo** | <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> | Redoes it, named the same way. Any new edit clears what could be redone. | There's something to redo |
| **Cut** | <kbd>⌘X</kbd> | Copies the selected clips and removes them, leaving a gap. If the copy fails, nothing is removed. See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/). | Something is selected |
| **Copy** | <kbd>⌘C</kbd> | Copies the selected clips. A selection across several tracks pastes back onto as many lanes. Pasted into another app, it's a short text summary. | Something is selected |
| **Paste** | <kbd>⌘V</kbd> | Pastes clips at the playhead, the earliest there and the others keeping their offsets. Nothing needs to be selected. It works between projects, matching media by path. | The clipboard holds Frame Job clips |
| **Paste Attributes** | <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd> | Puts the copied clip's look onto the selected clips. Only the earliest copied clip is read. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/). | Frame Job clips are copied and something is selected |
| **Paste Graphic Properties** | | Puts the copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips that use the same graphic. It beeps if the copied clip isn't a graphic. See [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/). | Frame Job clips are copied and a graphic clip is selected |
| **Duplicate** | <kbd>⌘D</kbd> | Copies the selected clips and places the copies after them. See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/). | Something is selected |
| **Delete** | <kbd>⌫</kbd> | Removes the selection and leaves a gap. With nothing selected it lifts the in/out range. With an action selected it removes that action, not its clip. With words selected in the Transcript tab it ripples them out. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/). | Something is selected, a range is set, or words are selected. Off while text is being edited, and while the curve plot holds a selected point, where <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point |
| **Ripple Delete** | <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | Removes the selection, or the in/out range when nothing is selected, and closes the gap. Words selected in the Transcript tab go first. | Something is selected, a range is set, or words are selected. Off while text is being edited |
| **Insert at Playhead** | | Inserts the file selected in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/), pushing later clips along. One undo step, "Insert". See [Insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/). | A file is selected in the Media tab, and it isn't a LUT |
| **Overwrite at Playhead** | | Places that file over whatever is there. One undo step, "Overwrite". | A file is selected in the Media tab, and it isn't a LUT |
| **Select All** | <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Selects every clip in the timeline you're editing. With the Transcript tab's words in focus, it selects every word. | Always |
| **Select After Playhead** | <kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd> | Selects every clip that starts at or after the playhead. | Always |
| **Select All on Track** | | Selects every clip on the current track. It beeps when the track is empty. | The timeline has clips |

Selecting adds no undo step. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).

## Insert menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_adjustment_clip', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'text_behind_subject']}
/>

No item in this menu has a key.

| Item | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Adjustment Clip** | Adds an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) over the in/out range. Without a range it covers the selected clips' span, and without a selection the whole timeline. It lands on the front track when it fits, and otherwise on a new front track named "Adjustment". One undo step. | No nest is open and the timeline isn't empty |
| **Graphic…** | Opens the Graphic dialog: the bundled templates by category, **This Project**'s own graphics and a looping preview, with **Insert**, **From File…** (a `.js` file, or a `.fjgraphic` to import) and **Export…** (saves the chosen one as a `.fjgraphic`). See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). | Always |
| **Text Behind Subject** | Puts a title on a new "Behind Subject" track above the camera clip at the playhead, behind the person, for 4 s or the rest of the clip. It turns [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on with Keep background when the clip doesn't have it. One undo step. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). | No nest is open, and a clip of a video file or a picture plays at the playhead with its picture on, on a shown track that isn't a matte track |

## Clip menu

The Clip menu sits between Insert and Track. See [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/).

## Track menu

<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'set_track', 'move_track']} />

Everything here but **New Track** and **Remove Empty Tracks** acts on the [current track](#how-to-read-these-tables). To act on a particular track, use that track's [context menu](/reference/context-menus/). Every item is available whenever a project window is in front with no sheet on it.

| Item | Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **New Track** | <kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd> | Adds a track at the front, the top lane. See [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/). |
| **Remove Track** | | Removes the current track. If it still holds clips you're asked first and told how many go with it, with **Remove** and **Cancel**. The last track can't be removed. |
| **Remove Empty Tracks** | | Removes every track that has no clips, keeping one if they're all empty. It beeps when there's nothing to remove. |
| **Hide Video** | | Hides or shows the track's picture. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| **Mute Audio** | | Mutes or unmutes the track's sound. Mute wins over Solo. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
| **Lock Track** | | Locks or unlocks the track, so its clips can't be edited. |
| **Solo** | | Plays only this track's sound. It's audio only. A checkmark shows when it's on, because a soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest. |
| **Mix…** | | Opens the track's mix panel: volume, pan, compressor and limiter. A timeline has one panel at a time, so opening it on another track closes the first. Inside an open nest its dynamics are disabled. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). |
| **Matte ▸** | | **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**. Makes the track a matte that cuts the track behind it, and a checkmark shows the mode. One undo step, "Track Matte", and choosing the mode it already has beeps. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |

**Hide Video**, **Mute Audio** and **Lock Track** show no checkmark here. The track's context menu shows one.

## Mark menu

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_range', 'set_playhead']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Marker** | <kbd>M</kbd> (key) | Adds a marker at the playhead, snapped to a frame. A second marker on the same frame beeps. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/). | No nest is open |
| **Set In** | <kbd>I</kbd> (key) | Sets the in point at the playhead. With no Out yet, the range runs to the end of the timeline. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/). | Always |
| **Set Out** | <kbd>O</kbd> (key) | Sets the out point at the playhead. With no In yet, the range starts at 0. | Always |
| **Clear Range** | <kbd>⌥X</kbd> | Clears the in/out range. | A range is set |
| **Next Marker** | | Moves the playhead to the next marker and pauses. It beeps past the last one. | The project has markers and no nest is open |
| **Previous Marker** | | Moves the playhead to the previous marker and pauses. It beeps before the first one. | The project has markers and no nest is open |

Setting In or Out adds no undo step.

## View menu

These items set how the window looks. Zoom always acts on the canvas. To zoom the timeline, use the timeline bar's controls or the [gestures](/reference/gestures/).

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Zoom In** | <kbd>⌘+</kbd> or <kbd>⌘=</kbd> | Zooms the canvas in one step. The steps are Fit, 50 %, 100 % and 200 %. See [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). | The canvas is below 200 % |
| **Zoom Out** | <kbd>⌘-</kbd> | Zooms the canvas out one step. | The canvas isn't at Fit |
| **Zoom to Fit** | <kbd>⌘0</kbd> | Fits the canvas to the preview again. | The canvas isn't at Fit |
| **Fit Timeline** | <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> (key) | Zooms the timeline to show the whole project and scrolls to the start. See [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/). | Always |
| **Snapping** | <kbd>N</kbd> (key) | Turns [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) on or off for the timeline and the canvas. A checkmark shows when it's on. | Always |
| **Safe Areas** | | Shows or hides the [safe-area guides](/canvas/safe-areas/) on the canvas, with a checkmark. | Always |
| **Hide Inspector** | <kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd> | Hides the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/). The item reads **Show Inspector** while it's hidden. | Always |
| **Transcript** | <kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd> | Shows the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/), ready for its keys, showing the inspector first if it's hidden. | Always |
| **Assistant** | <kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd> | Shows the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/) tab and puts the cursor in its message field, showing the inspector first if it's hidden. | Always |

These items change what you see in the preview, and none of them changes an export or a saved frame.

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,

---
title: "The Clip menu"
description: "Every command and submenu in the Clip menu, with its shortcut and what has to be true for it to be available."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Clip menu holds the commands that act on the selected clips. This page gives every item's exact title and shortcut, and what makes it available, so you can find a key or work out why something is greyed out.

The symbols and the **(key)** mark are explained in [How to read these tables](/reference/menus/#how-to-read-these-tables). Every item here is greyed out while a sheet is on the window.

## The Clip menu

From top to bottom, with lines dividing it into five groups after **Trim End to Playhead**, **Switch Angle ▸**, **Add Blurred Background** and **Label ▸**:

| Item | Keys | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Split at Shot Changes** | | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> (key) | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> (key) | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Detach Audio** | <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Attach Audio** | <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd> | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Normalize** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Enhance Voice** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Match Audio…** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Synchronize Audio** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Switch by Speaker…** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Add Action** | <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Auto Zoom…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Follow Subject…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Add Shortcut Overlays** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Speed Up Typing…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Speed…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Speed Ramp…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Close Gap** | | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Retime Range…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Remove Silences…** | | [Clean-up](#clean-up) |
| **Remove Filler Words…** | | [Clean-up](#clean-up) |
| **Transition ▸** | | [Transition](#transition) |
| **Motion ▸** | | [Motion](#motion) |
| **Look ▸** | | [Look](#look) |
| **Remove Background** | | [Remove Background](#remove-background) |
| **Camera Layout ▸** | | [Camera Layout](#camera-layout) |
| **Switch Angle ▸** | | [Switch Angle](#switch-angle) |
| **Add Background ▸** | | [Backgrounds](#backgrounds) |
| **Add Blurred Background** | | [Backgrounds](#backgrounds) |
| **Rename…** | <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> | [Rename and label](#rename-and-label) |
| **Label ▸** | | [Rename and label](#rename-and-label) |
| **Nest** | <kbd>⌘G</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |
| **Un-nest** | <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |
| **Open Nest** | <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |
| **Close Nest** | <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |

Most items have no key, because every bare letter belongs to the editor and a menu key with no modifier would take it.

## Cutting and trimming

<AtAGlance tools={['split', 'split_at_shots', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'freeze_frame', 'close_gap']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> | Cuts the selected clips at the playhead. With nothing selected, it cuts every unlocked clip under the playhead. See [Split clips](/editing/splitting/). | The timeline has any clip |
| **Split at Shot Changes** | | Cuts each selected clip of a video file at every hard cut in the part it plays, as one undo step. The Analyzing sheet shows while the cuts are found on this Mac. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/). | A selected clip shows a video file's picture |
| **Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> (key) | Trims the selected clips' starts to the playhead. A linked sound half trims alone. See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> (key) | Trims the selected clips' ends to the playhead. A linked sound half trims alone. | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> | Holds the frame under the playhead as a still clip, 2 s long, in a gap opened there. It acts on the first selected clip under the playhead, and only on a media clip. See [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Close Gap** | | Closes the gap under the playhead on the current track, and everything from the far side slides left across every unlocked track. See [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/). | The timeline has clips |

## Sound

<AtAGlance
  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio', 'switch_by_speaker']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Detach Audio** | <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> | Moves a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below, linked to it. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | Something is selected |
| **Attach Audio** | <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd> | Merges a detached sound back into its picture. | A selected clip is linked to its detached sound or picture |
| **Normalize** | | Sets the selected clips' volume to a loudness (the default, turning a clip's limiter on when its peaks need it) or a peak, by the mode chosen in the Volume section's Normalize row. A clip with processing is measured through it under the Measuring Sound sheet. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/). | A selected clip plays sound and isn't a nest |
| **Enhance Voice** | | Sets the selected clips up for speech from their own measurements, as one undo step. See [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/). | A selected clip plays sound and isn't a nest |
| **Match Audio…** | | Gives the selected clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, chosen in a sheet, measured under the Measuring Sound sheet. See [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/). | Two or more selected clips play sound, not counting nests |
| **Synchronize Audio** | | Lines up the selected clips by their sound. A weak match asks you first. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/). | Two or more selected clips play sound, not counting nests |
| **Switch by Speaker…** | | Cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as one undo step. Run **Synchronize Audio** first. See [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/). | The selected clips with a picture sit on two or more tracks and a selected clip has its sound on. It works inside a nest |

## Actions and speed

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_action', 'auto_zoom', 'reframe_clip', 'add_shortcut_overlays', 'speed_up_typing', 'set_speed', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Action** | <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> | Adds an action at the playhead, 1 s long with an empty end state. Frame Job won't add one that would overlap another action or run past the clip's end. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Auto Zoom…** | | Zooms the selected screen recordings in at their clicks and typing and back out after, as ordinary actions, in one undo step, "Auto Zoom". See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/). | Every selected clip plays a movie that has a cursor file. It works inside a nest |
| **Follow Subject…** | | Frames each selected movie clip on its subject, found on this Mac, with eased moves on its action lane and a blurred copy on a Backgrounds track where it shows the whole picture, in one undo step. See [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/). | A selected clip plays a movie. It works inside a nest |
| **Add Shortcut Overlays** | | Shows each keyboard shortcut recorded in the selected screen recordings as keycaps at the moment it was pressed, on a "Shortcuts" track, in one undo step. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). | Every selected clip plays a movie that has a cursor file, and Frame Job isn't already reading the files. It works inside a nest |

| **Speed…** | | Sets the selected clips' playback rate through a sheet, ×0.1 to ×1000. See [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/). | The selection includes a clip that plays a media file |
| **Speed Ramp…** | | Puts a speed ramp preset on one selected media clip. See [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/). | Exactly one clip is selected and it plays a media file |
| **Retime Range…** | | Plays the in/out range faster or slower on every unlocked track and moves what follows to stay in step, in one undo step, "Retime Range". See [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). | An in/out range is set. It works inside a nest |

## Clean-up

<AtAGlance
  tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
  needs="Remove Filler Words… needs your AssemblyAI key, unless a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words."
/>

| Item | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove Silences…** | Finds silent stretches and removes them, through a sheet. It needs no key. See [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/). | A clip plays sound |
| **Remove Filler Words…** | Finds "um"s and "uh"s and removes them, through a sheet. See [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/). | A clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on, and either your AssemblyAI key is set or a file in scope has a transcript made with filler words |

When the key is all that's missing, the item is greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**, and its tooltip says where to set the key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

## Transition

<AtAGlance tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition']} />

**Transition ▸** sets the transition into the clip. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).

The rows are **Cross Dissolve**, **Fade Through Black**, **Fade Through White**, **Push Left**, **Push Right**, **Push Up**, **Push Down**, **Wipe**, **Slide**, **Zoom**, **Wipe Left**, **Wipe Up** and **Wipe Down**, then **None**. A checkmark shows the selected clip's transition.

| Row | Available when |
| --- | --- |
| A transition | A selected clip has room for one, meaning an overlap or a hard cut. Other selected clips are skipped. |
| **None** | Something is selected, so a stored transition the timeline doesn't draw can always be cleared. |

At a hard cut it adds a transition 0.5 s long, snapped to frames. Where neither side of the cut has a frame to spare, a sheet says so and offers **Shift Clips Left**.

## Motion

<AtAGlance tools="set_video" />

**Motion ▸** sets how the clip enters, leaves and moves, and previews the result. Every item is available when a selected clip shows a picture. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

| Item | Rows |
| --- | --- |
| **In ▸** | **Fade**, **Zoom In**, **Zoom Out**, **Slide Left**, **Slide Right**, **Slide Up**, **Slide Down**, **Spin**, **Pop**, then **None** |
| **Out ▸** | The same as **In ▸** |
| **During ▸** | **Pulse**, **Shake**, **Spin**, **Bounce**, **Drift**, then **None** |
| **Preview** | Sets the in/out range to the first selected clip with a picture, turns Loop on and plays it. The range and Loop stay set afterwards. |

In each submenu a checkmark shows the kind every selected clip has. An In or Out kind with a length of zero reads "Fade (inactive)", or "Fade (some inactive)" when only some of the selected clips with that kind have zero length.

Every During motion starts from where the clip is placed, so the clip's first frame sits exactly there.

## Look

<AtAGlance tools="set_video" />

**Look ▸** puts a look or a LUT on the clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

The rows are **Warm**, **Cool**, **Teal & Orange**, **Vivid**, **Faded**, **Vintage**, **Dramatic** and **Black & White**, then the project's `.cube` LUTs in Media list order when it has any, then **None**. The LUT rows are written each time the menu opens.

A checkmark marks a look every selected clip has, and a dash marks one only some of them have. Each clip keeps its amount, and a clip with no look starts at full strength.

It's available when a selected clip shows a picture from a file, or is an adjustment clip.

## Remove Background

<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'analyze_cutout']} />

**Remove Background** keeps the person and removes the rest of the picture, or turns that off. It has no key. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).

It's checked when every selected clip has it, and shows a dash when some do. With every clip it can act on already cut out, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without, and each clip already cut out keeps its values.

It's available when a selected clip plays a video file, is a freeze frame of one, or is a picture.

## Camera Layout

<AtAGlance tools="switch_layout" />

**Camera Layout ▸** lays out the camera and the screen behind it at the playhead, eased over half a second and held until the next switch. One undo step, "Camera Layout". See [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/).

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Corner ▸** | The camera in a box in the corner you pick, with the screen at its full placement. The box is a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall and 5 % in from the edges. |
| **Rounded Corner ▸** | The same with rounded corners. |
| **Circle ▸** | The same as a circle. |
| **Side by Side** | The screen fitted in the left two-thirds, and the camera cropped to fill the right third, with margins and a small radius. |
| **Stacked** | The screen across the top, and the camera filling the rest below. |
| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |
| **Screen Only** | Hides the camera where it is. |

**Corner ▸**, **Rounded Corner ▸** and **Circle ▸** each hold **Bottom Right**, **Bottom Left**, **Top Right** and **Top Left**.

The camera's crop is centred on the person when the camera's masks are cached. A zoom in the way brings up a sheet offering **Nest and Switch**.

It's available with two selected clips with a picture on different tracks, one selected clip with a picture, or, with nothing selected, a clip at the playhead on a track named "Camera". The camera has to contain the playhead. It works inside a nest.

## Switch Angle

<AtAGlance tools="switch_angle" />

**Switch Angle ▸** re-picks the selected shot from another camera track that covers it, keeping its span, its switches and its dissolves, as one undo step. The new pieces are selected. See [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

It has one row per track covering the shot's whole span, written each time the menu opens. There are up to nine, front first, named after their tracks, and tracks that share a name add their position, as in "Camera (2)". With no track to offer, the menu shows **No Covering Angle**, which is never available.

A row is available when exactly one clip is selected, its track isn't locked, it isn't linked to a detached sound, and that row's track still covers it with video clips. It works inside a nest.

## Backgrounds

<AtAGlance tools={['add_background', 'add_blurred_background']} />

Both commands put something on a new track behind everything. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).

| Item | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Background ▸ Solid Color** | Adds a canvas-sized white plate the length of the timeline, selected so you can recolour it in the Clip tab's Fill row. There's no dialog. | Always |
| **Add Background ▸ Image…** | Adds a picture you choose, at Fill scale, the length of the timeline. It takes images only. Importing and placing are one undo step. | Always |
| **Add Blurred Background** | Adds a blurred copy of the picture at the same start, duration, speed and source window. The copy is muted, and has none of the clip's transition, actions or label. | Exactly one clip is selected and it has a picture size: a video, image, still, shape or graphic clip. Greyed for a nest, text, adjustment or audio-only clip |

**Add Background ▸** needs no selection.

## Rename and label

<AtAGlance tools="set_clip" />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rename…** | <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> | Renames the selected clip in place on the timeline. It's also the way to rename a nest clip, because double-clicking one opens it. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/). | Something is selected |
| **Label ▸** | | **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue** and **Purple**, each with its colour dot, then **None**. A checkmark shows the label the selected clips share. One undo step, "Label Clip", and a colour every selected clip already carries beeps. | Something is selected |

## Nests

<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest', 'set_scope']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nest** | <kbd>⌘G</kbd> | Wraps the selected clips into one nest clip, which is selected afterwards. The nest's canvas is frozen at the project's current size. See [Nests](/editing/nests/). | Something is selected, other than a single nest clip on its own |
| **Un-nest** | <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> | Breaks a nest clip back into its clips. The nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume are lost. | The selection includes a nest clip |
| **Open Nest** | <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | Goes inside the selected nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/). | Exactly one clip is selected and it's a nest clip |
| **Close Nest** | <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | Comes back out by one level. | A nest is open |

**Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are greyed while you're typing in a text field.

- [Menus](/reference/menus/)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
- [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/)

In each submenu a checkmark shows the kind every selected clip has. An In or Out kind with a length of zero reads "Fade (inactive)", or "Fade (some inactive)" when only some of the selected clips with that kind have zero length.

Every During motion starts from where the clip is placed, so the clip's first frame sits exactly there.

## Look

<AtAGlance tools="set_video" />

**Look ▸** puts a look or a LUT on the clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

The rows are **Warm**, **Cool**, **Teal & Orange**, **Vivid**, **Faded**, **Vintage**, **Dramatic** and **Black & White**, then the project's `.cube` LUTs in Media list order when it has any, then **None**. The LUT rows are written each time the menu opens.

A checkmark marks a look every selected clip has, and a dash marks one only some of them have. Each clip keeps its amount, and a clip with no look starts at full strength.

It's available when a selected clip shows a picture from a file, or is an adjustment clip.

## Remove Background

<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'analyze_cutout']} />

**Remove Background** keeps the person and removes the rest of the picture, or turns that off. It has no key. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).

It's checked when every selected clip has it, and shows a dash when some do. With every clip it can act on already cut out, it turns them all off. Otherwise it turns on the ones without, and each clip already cut out keeps its values.

It's available when a selected clip plays a video file, is a freeze frame of one, or is a picture.

## Camera Layout

<AtAGlance tools="switch_layout" />

**Camera Layout ▸** lays out the camera and the screen behind it at the playhead, eased over half a second and held until the next switch. One undo step, "Camera Layout". See [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/).

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Corner ▸** | The camera in a box in the corner you pick, with the screen at its full placement. The box is a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall and 5 % in from the edges. |
| **Rounded Corner ▸** | The same with rounded corners. |
| **Circle ▸** | The same as a circle. |
| **Side by Side** | The screen fitted in the left two-thirds, and the camera cropped to fill the right third, with margins and a small radius. |
| **Stacked** | The screen across the top, and the camera filling the rest below. |
| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |
| **Screen Only** | Hides the camera where it is. |

**Corner ▸**, **Rounded Corner ▸** and **Circle ▸** each hold **Bottom Right**, **Bottom Left**, **Top Right** and **Top Left**.

The camera's crop is centred on the person when the camera's masks are cached. A zoom in the way brings up a sheet offering **Nest and Switch**.

It's available with two selected clips with a picture on different tracks, one selected clip with a picture, or, with nothing selected, a clip at the playhead on a track named "Camera". The camera has to contain the playhead. It works inside a nest.

## Switch Angle

<AtAGlance tools="switch_angle" />

**Switch Angle ▸** re-picks the selected shot from another camera track that covers it, keeping its span, its switches and its dissolves, as one undo step. The new pieces are selected. See [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

It has one row per track covering the shot's whole span, written each time the menu opens. There are up to nine, front first, named after their tracks, and tracks that share a name add their position, as in "Camera (2)". With no track to offer, the menu shows **No Covering Angle**, which is never available.

A row is available when exactly one clip is selected, its track isn't locked, it isn't linked to a detached sound, and that row's track still covers it with video clips. It works inside a nest.

## Backgrounds

<AtAGlance tools={['add_background', 'add_blurred_background']} />

Both commands put something on a new track behind everything. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).

| Item | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Background ▸ Solid Color** | Adds a canvas-sized white plate the length of the timeline, selected so you can recolour it in the Clip tab's Fill row. There's no dialog. | Always |
| **Add Background ▸ Image…** | Adds a picture you choose, at Fill scale, the length of the timeline. It takes images only. Importing and placing are one undo step. | Always |
| **Add Blurred Background** | Adds a blurred copy of the picture at the same start, duration, speed and source window. The copy is muted, and has none of the clip's transition, actions or label. | Exactly one clip is selected and it has a picture size: a video, image, still, shape or graphic clip. Greyed for a nest, text, adjustment or audio-only clip |

**Add Background ▸** needs no selection.

## Rename and label

<AtAGlance tools="set_clip" />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rename…** | <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> | Renames the selected clip in place on the timeline. It's also the way to rename a nest clip, because double-clicking one opens it. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/). | Something is selected |
| **Label ▸** | | **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue** and **Purple**, each with its colour dot, then **None**. A checkmark shows the label the selected clips share. One undo step, "Label Clip", and a colour every selected clip already carries beeps. | Something is selected |

## Nests

<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest', 'set_scope']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nest** | <kbd>⌘G</kbd> | Wraps the selected clips into one nest clip, which is selected afterwards. The nest's canvas is frozen at the project's current size. See [Nests](/editing/nests/). | Something is selected, other than a single nest clip on its own |
| **Un-nest** | <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> | Breaks a nest clip back into its clips. The nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume are lost. | The selection includes a nest clip |
| **Open Nest** | <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | Goes inside the selected nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/). | Exactly one clip is selected and it's a nest clip |
| **Close Nest** | <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | Comes back out by one level. | A nest is open |

**Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are greyed while you're typing in a text field.

## Related

- [Menus](/reference/menus/)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
- [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/)

---
title: "The Clip menu"
description: "Every command and submenu in the Clip menu, with its shortcut and what has to be true for it to be available."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Clip menu holds the commands that act on the selected clips. This page gives every item's exact title and shortcut, and what makes it available, so you can find a key or work out why something is greyed out.

The symbols and the **(key)** mark are explained in [How to read these tables](/reference/menus/#how-to-read-these-tables). Every item here is greyed out while a sheet is on the window.

## The Clip menu

From top to bottom, with lines dividing it into five groups after **Trim End to Playhead**, **Switch Angle ▸**, **Add Blurred Background** and **Label ▸**:

| Item | Keys | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Split at Shot Changes** | | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> (key) | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> (key) | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Detach Audio** | <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Attach Audio** | <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd> | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Normalize** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Enhance Voice** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Match Audio…** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Synchronize Audio** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Switch by Speaker…** | | [Sound](#sound) |
| **Add Action** | <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Auto Zoom…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Follow Subject…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Add Shortcut Overlays** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Speed Up Typing…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Speed…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Speed Ramp…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Close Gap** | | [Cutting and trimming](#cutting-and-trimming) |
| **Retime Range…** | | [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed) |
| **Remove Silences…** | | [Clean-up](#clean-up) |
| **Remove Filler Words…** | | [Clean-up](#clean-up) |
| **Transition ▸** | | [Transition](#transition) |
| **Motion ▸** | | [Motion](#motion) |
| **Look ▸** | | [Look](#look) |
| **Remove Background** | | [Remove Background](#remove-background) |
| **Camera Layout ▸** | | [Camera Layout](#camera-layout) |
| **Switch Angle ▸** | | [Switch Angle](#switch-angle) |
| **Add Background ▸** | | [Backgrounds](#backgrounds) |
| **Add Blurred Background** | | [Backgrounds](#backgrounds) |
| **Rename…** | <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> | [Rename and label](#rename-and-label) |
| **Label ▸** | | [Rename and label](#rename-and-label) |
| **Nest** | <kbd>⌘G</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |
| **Un-nest** | <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |
| **Open Nest** | <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |
| **Close Nest** | <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | [Nests](#nests) |

Most items have no key, because every bare letter belongs to the editor and a menu key with no modifier would take it.

## Cutting and trimming

<AtAGlance tools={['split', 'split_at_shots', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'freeze_frame', 'close_gap']} />

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> | Cuts the selected clips at the playhead. With nothing selected, it cuts every unlocked clip under the playhead. See [Split clips](/editing/splitting/). | The timeline has any clip |
| **Split at Shot Changes** | | Cuts each selected clip of a video file at every hard cut in the part it plays, as one undo step. The Analyzing sheet shows while the cuts are found on this Mac. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/). | A selected clip shows a video file's picture |
| **Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> (key) | Trims the selected clips' starts to the playhead. A linked sound half trims alone. See [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> (key) | Trims the selected clips' ends to the playhead. A linked sound half trims alone. | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> | Holds the frame under the playhead as a still clip, 2 s long, in a gap opened there. It acts on the first selected clip under the playhead, and only on a media clip. See [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |
| **Close Gap** | | Closes the gap under the playhead on the current track, and everything from the far side slides left across every unlocked track. See [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/). | The timeline has clips |

## Sound

<AtAGlance
  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio', 'switch_by_speaker']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Detach Audio** | <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> | Moves a clip's sound onto its own clip on the track below, linked to it. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | Something is selected |
| **Attach Audio** | <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd> | Merges a detached sound back into its picture. | A selected clip is linked to its detached sound or picture |
| **Normalize** | | Sets the selected clips' volume to a loudness (the default, turning a clip's limiter on when its peaks need it) or a peak, by the mode chosen in the Volume section's Normalize row. A clip with processing is measured through it under the Measuring Sound sheet. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/). | A selected clip plays sound and isn't a nest |
| **Enhance Voice** | | Sets the selected clips up for speech from their own measurements, as one undo step. See [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/). | A selected clip plays sound and isn't a nest |
| **Match Audio…** | | Gives the selected clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, chosen in a sheet, measured under the Measuring Sound sheet. See [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/). | Two or more selected clips play sound, not counting nests |
| **Synchronize Audio** | | Lines up the selected clips by their sound. A weak match asks you first. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/). | Two or more selected clips play sound, not counting nests |
| **Switch by Speaker…** | | Cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as one undo step. Run **Synchronize Audio** first. See [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/). | The selected clips with a picture sit on two or more tracks and a selected clip has its sound on. It works inside a nest |

## Actions and speed

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_action', 'auto_zoom', 'reframe_clip', 'add_shortcut_overlays', 'speed_up_typing', 'set_speed', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range']}
/>

| Item | Keys | What it does | Available when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add Action** | <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> | Adds an action at the playhead, 1 s long with an empty end state. Frame Job won't add one that would overlap another action or run past the clip's end. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). | A selected clip is under the playhead |

| **Follow Subject…** | | Frames each selected movie clip on its subject, found on this Mac, with eased moves on its action lane and a blurred copy on a Backgrounds track where it shows the whole picture, in one undo step. | **Add Shortcut Overlays** | | Shows each keyboard shortcut recorded in the selected screen recordings as keycaps at the moment it was pressed, on a "Shortcuts" track, in one undo step. | **Speed Ramp…** | | Puts a speed ramp preset on one selected media clip. See [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/). | Exactly one clip is selected and it plays a media file |
| **Retime Range…** | | Plays the in/out range faster or slower on every unlocked track and moves what follows to stay in step, in one undo step, "Retime Range". See [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/). | An in/out range is set. It works inside a nest |
